newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline rises but barge market stays lethargi.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline rises but barge market stays lethargi.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices rose moderately on Wednesday but traders said the barge market was very quiet and lethargic after recent volatility.
"The market is at a stand-off because we were down for two to three days and NYMEX showed an uptrend yesterday," a barge trader said. "There is no buying interest at all."
"I don't see any reason why prices went up today," said another barge trader. "If you look at the API stats very closely you will see there is not much change from last week."
The American Petroleum Institute said U.S. gasoline inventories last week fell 535,000 barrels to 187.3 million, with the deficit to a year ago at 4.7 million.
He said another prop knocked away from the gasoline market was news that a possible oil export strike at Mina al-Ahmadi by Kuwaiti oil workers was suspended.
Kuwaiti National Petroleum Co officials said there was no disruption to exports at Ahmadi, which has a 420,000 barrel per day refinery and a main oil export terminal.
Traders said arbitrage opportunities to the U.S. this week steadied cargo prices but did not filter through to barges, where demand appeared satisfied heading into the U.K. budget on November 26.
"Obviously the barge market is not following the latest...NYMEX rally," a trader said.
Eurograde barges were heard at $219 and $221.50 with last offers near $219 to $221 fob ARA, against offers late Tuesday at $214, traders said.
